title: Understand the difference between JDK, JRE, and JVM
answer: The JVM, JRE, and JDK are related but serve different purposes. The JVM is the execution engine that loads, verifies, and runs Java bytecode while providing runtime services such as memory management and JIT compilation. The JRE is the runtime environment needed to run Java applications: conceptually it includes the JVM plus the standard runtime libraries and supporting files. The JDK is the development kit; it includes the runtime capabilities plus developer tools such as `javac`, `javap`, `javadoc`, and other utilities used to compile, inspect, package, and troubleshoot Java software. In modern distributions, teams commonly install a JDK rather than a separately packaged JRE. For AeroTopo, Java 21 JDK provides the development toolchain, while its JVM executes the compiled application.

steps.title: Inspect installed JDKs in IntelliJ
steps.question: A developer may have several Java installations on one machine, but the term JDK refers to the complete development kit rather than only the runtime process. When IntelliJ shows installed SDK entries, what capabilities distinguish a JDK from the JVM that eventually executes AeroTopo bytecode?
steps.why: A JDK includes development tools and a runtime, while the JVM is the execution engine inside that runtime environment.
steps.why_te: Installed JDK versions ikkada kanipistayi. Machine lo multiple JDKs undachu. Current project ki ye JDK select chesamo separate ga check cheyyali.

steps.title: Confirm AeroTopo uses Java 21
steps.question: Installing a JDK does not automatically make every project use it, because the IDE and build must select a concrete Java home and language level. Why does AeroTopo explicitly use Java 21 as its Project SDK when discussing the responsibilities of the JDK?
steps.why: Project SDK selection ties the development toolchain to a specific JDK installation instead of an arbitrary machine default.
steps.why_te: Project SDK ikkada kanipistundi. AeroTopo Java 21 use chestunda ani check cheyyachu. Wrong JDK unte compile errors ravachu.

steps.title: Open the terminal
steps.question: The easiest way to distinguish JDK, JRE, and JVM is to observe development commands and runtime commands separately rather than treating Java as one executable. Why should the IntelliJ terminal be opened before comparing `javac`, `java`, and the JVM runtime itself?
steps.why: The terminal exposes distinct tools in the Java installation and makes their responsibilities observable.
steps.why_te: IntelliJ terminal ni open chesi commands run cheddam. Terminal lo `javac` mariyu `java` separate commands ga run chesthe development toolchain mariyu runtime responsibilities clear ga kanipistayi. JDK, JRE, JVM concepts okate thing kaadani practical ga observe cheyyachu.

steps.title: Verify javac
steps.question: The `javac` compiler is a development tool used to convert Java source into class-file bytecode, so it belongs to the JDK side of the platform. What does checking `javac --version` prove that checking the running JVM alone would not prove?
steps.why: It proves that the development compiler is installed and identifies the JDK toolchain version available to compile source.
steps.why_te: Ee command run chesi output ni chudandi. `javac --version` compiler tool actual ga install ayindani mariyu ye JDK version source compilation kosam use avutundo confirm chestundi. JVM runtime version chudatam okkate compiler availability ni prove cheyyadu.

steps.title: Verify java runtime
steps.question: The `java` launcher starts a Java runtime and ultimately a JVM process capable of loading class files, which is a different responsibility from compiling source code. What does `java --version` tell you about the runtime environment selected for execution on this machine?
steps.why: It identifies the active runtime implementation and Java version used to launch Java applications.
steps.why_te: Ee command run chesi output ni chudandi. `java --version` current shell nundi application run cheyyadaniki use ayye runtime version ni chupistundi. Idi source compile chese `javac` responsibility kaadu.

steps.title: Inspect the JVM
steps.question: The JVM is narrower than the whole JDK because its job begins after compiled bytecode is available. When IntelliJ visualizes class loading, verification, interpretation or JIT compilation, and garbage collection, which part of the Java platform stack are you observing?
steps.why: Those services belong to JVM execution rather than source compilation or the complete developer kit.
steps.why_te: JVM view lo class loading, bytecode verification and JIT steps kanipistayi. Java program run ayye time lo JVM ee work chestundi.

steps.title: Inspect runtime libraries
steps.question: A runtime environment needs more than an execution engine because Java applications also depend on standard runtime classes and project libraries. Why does viewing the classpath help explain the conceptual role traditionally associated with the JRE around the JVM?
steps.why: The runtime environment combines the JVM with the libraries and resources required by executing applications.
steps.why_te: Classpath lo application classes and required libraries ekkada unnayo kanipistayi. Dependency missing ayithe program start avvakapovachu.

data.purpose: Runtime classes and libraries available to the JVM

steps.title: Verify the full stack
steps.question: A Java project is healthy only when the JDK compiler tools, runtime environment, JVM, dependencies, and build configuration cooperate instead of being individually installed but inconsistent. Why is a successful Maven test run a practical final check of the JDK/JRE/JVM relationship in AeroTopo?
steps.why: The build exercises compilation and runtime together under the project's selected toolchain.
steps.why_te: Maven goal run chesi build result ni chudandi. Maven test run compilation mariyu runtime stages renditini same project toolchain lo exercise chestundi. JDK tools, runtime/JVM mariyu dependencies practical ga kalisi work chestunnayi ani final evidence vastundi.
